value="<div>Im Zielsystem werden alle relevanten Ziele, deren Randbedingungen,&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Abhängigkeiten und Wechselwirkungen beschrieben. Das Zielsystem enthält die&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">explizite Dokumentation der zur Realisierung nötigen Informationen. Die Elemente&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">im Zielsystem müssen nachvollziehbar und begründet sein. Es enthält nur&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Informationen, keine physischen Objekte, und ist damit der Speicher der gesicherten&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Erkenntnisse und Planung der Produktentstehung.</span></div><div>(Meboldt 2008)</div><div><br></div><div>Hypothese:</div><div>Das Zielsystem wird repräsentiert durch alle Elemente die zur logischen Produktstruktur der Produktarchitektur führen.</div><div>Die Explizierung bzw. die Gestalt erfolgt im Produkt Typ und den Konkreten Assemblies, sowie Komponenten.</div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="160" width="190" x="-395" y="-140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell value="<div><div>System Context Diagrams ... represent all external entities that may interact with a system ... Such a diagram pictures the system at the center, with no details of its interior structure, surrounded by all its interacting systems, environments and activities. The objective of the system context diagram is to focus attention on external factors and events that should be considered in developing a complete set of systems requirements and constraints.</div><div>(Alexander Kossiakoff, William N. Sweet (2011). Systems Engineering: Principles and Practices p. 266)</div></div><div><br></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="120" width="190" x="10" y="-670" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="lWb6erf_lHs08Pngw-pu-54" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=8;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;" value="<div>Relations are based on sysml:</div><div>allocate</div><div>derive</div><div>satisfy</div><div>refine</div><div>trace</div><div>composition</div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="160" width="325" x="430" y="-720" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="5lIMCNXJcWRLcvxoPiYy-273" parent="1" style="shape=image;verticalLabelPosition=bottom;labelBackgroundColor=default;verticalAlign=top;aspect=fixed;imageAspect=0;image=data:image/png,;" value="" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="130" width="220.83" x="514" y="-699" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="lWb6erf_lHs08Pngw-pu-55" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=6;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;" value="<div><div>A stakeholder need is an element type in the system</div><div>of objectives. It is an often abstract technical or</div><div>business expectation towards a (sub)system, inde</div><div>pendent of the technical solution and non-binding</div><div>for the realization..</div><div>(Kubin doi: 10.1109/SysCon53073.2023.10131072)</div></div><div><br></div><div><br></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="80" width="150" x="490" y="-290" as="geometry" /> value="<div>The Element Variation is composed of a sum of variations derived from the reference system which has a sum of reference system elements.</div><div><br></div><div>Example:</div><div>Product Variant: Electrical Car</div><div>ReferenceSystem: Contains Battery and ICE Vehicles (Petrol Car for example) as Elements</div><div>Battery can be derived as a AttributeVariation</div><div>ICE value="<div><div><div><div>The Model of PGE – Product Generation Engineering describes the development of a new product as the development of a new product generation G n based on a product-specific reference system R n that summarizes e.g., existing (sub-)systems, concepts, or architectures as reference system elements.</div><div>https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000163804</div></div></div></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="240" x="570" y="375" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell value="<div>The previous product generation is one possible source of Referemce System Elements for the reference system of the current generation.</div><div><br></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="105" width="100" x="130" y="430" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="BtcpH7N1x9v3J88vtf7i-12" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=5;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;" value="<div>A member of a set of elements that constitutes a system. A system element is a discrete part of a system that can be implemented to fulfill specified requirements. A system element can be hardware, software, data, humans, processes (e.g., processes for providing service to users), procedures (e.g., operator instructions), facilities, materials, and naturally occurring entities (e.g., water, organisms, minerals), or any combination. (ISO/IEC 15288:2015)</div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;">https://sebokwiki.org/wiki/System_Element_(glossary)</span></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="290" x="420" y="140" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="BtcpH7N1x9v3J88vtf7i-13" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=6;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;" value="<div>Jede Produktgeneration</div><div>hat ihr eigenes Referenz-system. (Albers 2019)&nbsp;</div><div>https://publikationen.</div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;">bibliothek.kit.edu/1000093227</span></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="60" width="140" x="400" y="250" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="BtcpH7N1x9v3J88vtf7i-14" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=5;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;" value="<div>Das Referenzsystem für die Entwicklung einer neuen Produktgeneration ist ein System, dessen&nbsp;<span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">Elemente bereits existierenden oder bereits geplanten sozio-technischen Systemen und der&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">zugehörigen Dokumentation entstammen und Grundlage und Ausgangspunkt der Entwicklung</span></div><div>der neuen Produktgeneration sind. (Albers 2019)</div><div>https://publikationen.bibliothek.kit.edu/1000093227<br></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="70" width="170" x="375" y="360" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="BtcpH7N1x9v3J88vtf7i-15" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=6;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;" value="<div>All variations by which a new system is developed together form an operator V that describes the emergence of a new system generation based on the underlying reference system R&nbsp;</div><div><span style="background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(255, 255, 255));">(https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-78368-6_2)&nbsp;</span></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="200" x="170" y="290" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="0OTRnz_N1wjVSA4-4pHk-2" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=6;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=middle;" value="<div><span><span style="white-space: pre;">	<span style="white-space: pre;">	</span>S</span>ystem Architecture: IEEE standard 1471-2000 defines architecture as "the fundamental organization <span style="white-space: pre;">	</span><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span>of a system embodied in its components, their relationships to each other, and to the environment, and <span style="white-space: pre;">	</span><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span>the principles guiding its design and evolution" (IEEE 2000). Similarly, ISO/IEC 42010-2011 defines <span style="white-space: pre;">	</span><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span>architecture as "fundamental concepts or properties of a system in its environment embodied in its <span style="white-space: pre;">	</span><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span>elements, relationships, and in the principles of its design and evolution" (ISO/IEC 2011).</span></div><div><span style="background-color: transparent;"><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span><span style="white-space: pre;">	</span>https://sebokwiki.org/wiki/System_Architecture_Design_Definition</span></div>" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry height="50" width="300" x="-9" y="110" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="0OTRnz_N1wjVSA4-4pHk-3" edge="1" parent="1" source="5lIMCNXJcWRLcvxoPiYy-287" style="edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=0;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;html=1;jumpStyle=arc;" target="5lIMCNXJcWRLcvxoPiYy-82"> <mxGeometry relative="1" as="geometry"> <Array as="points"> <mxPoint x="430" y="90" /> <mxPoint x="710" y="90" /> <mxPoint x="710" y="-80" /> <mxPoint x="430" y="-80" /> </Array> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="0OTRnz_N1wjVSA4-4pHk-4" connectable="0" parent="0OTRnz_N1wjVSA4-4pHk-3" style="edgeLabel;html=1;align=center;verticalAlign=middle;resizable=0;points=[];" value="product:traceToSystemRequirement" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry relative="1" x="0.4189" y="-1" as="geometry"> <mxPoint x="-54" as="offset" /> </mxGeometry> </mxCell> <mxCell id="0OTRnz_N1wjVSA4-4pHk-7" parent="1" style="shape=note;whiteSpace=wrap;html=1;backgroundOutline=1;darkOpacity=0.05;fillStyle=solid;direction=west;gradientDirection=north;shadow=1;size=20;autosizeText=1;fontSize=9;align=left;labelPosition=center;verticalLabelPosition=middle;verticalAlign=top;fillColor=#d80073;fontColor=#ffffff;strokeColor=#A50040;" value="Alle grünen Elemente dienen zur Beschreibung der Systemarchitektur. div.div: Im Zielsystem werden alle relevanten Ziele, deren Randbedingungen, Abhängigkeiten und Wechselwirkungen beschrieben. Das Zielsystem enthält die explizite Dokumentation der zur Realisierung nötigen Informationen. Die Elemente im Zielsystem müssen nachvollziehbar und begründet sein. Es enthält nur Informationen, keine physischen Objekte, und ist damit der Speicher der gesicherten Erkenntnisse und Planung der Produktentstehung.
Das Zielsystem wird repräsentiert durch alle Elemente die zur logischen Produktstruktur der Produktarchitektur führen.
Die Explizierung bzw. die Gestalt erfolgt im Produkt Typ und den Konkreten Assemblies, sowie Komponenten.

div.div: System Context Diagrams ... represent all external entities that may interact with a system ... Such a diagram pictures the system at the center, with no details of its interior structure, surrounded by all its interacting systems, environments and activities. The objective of the system context diagram is to focus attention on external factors and events that should be considered in developing a complete set of systems requirements and constraints.
(Alexander Kossiakoff, William N. Sweet (2011). Systems Engineering: Principles and Practices p. 266)

div.div:
Product Generation Contains:
Represents System of Interest
Contains System Life Cycle
Contains Architecture
Contains Environment ...
ISO 15288:2015: System-of-Interest: system whose life cycle is under consideration in the context of this International Standard. This enables all of the system live cycle processes that are identified in ISO 15288:2015 to be considered as part of the system life cycle of a designed physical system.
https://system.desc.systems/Content/System/CM_System-of-Interest.htm

div.div: The Model of PGE – Product Generation Engineering describes the development of a new product as the development of a new product generation G n based on a product-specific reference system R n that summarizes e.g., existing (sub-)systems, concepts, or architectures as reference system elements.

div.div: A member of a set of elements that constitutes a system. A system element is a discrete part of a system that can be implemented to fulfill specified requirements. A system element can be hardware, software, data, humans, processes (e.g., processes for providing service to users), procedures (e.g., operator instructions), facilities, materials, and naturally occurring entities (e.g., water, organisms, minerals), or any combination. (ISO/IEC 15288:2015)

div.span: System Architecture: IEEE standard 1471-2000 defines architecture as "the fundamental organization of a system embodied in its components, their relationships to each other, and to the environment, and the principles guiding its design and evolution" (IEEE 2000). Similarly, ISO/IEC 42010-2011 defines architecture as "fundamental concepts or properties of a system in its environment embodied in its elements, relationships, and in the principles of its design and evolution" (ISO/IEC 2011).

div.div:
Alle grünen Elemente dienen zur Beschreibung der Systemarchitektur. Die gesamte Systemarchitektur selbst kann nicht beschrieben werden, da die Ontologie ein Bestandteil der Systemarchtiektur ist. (Holt und Perry (2018) )
Die Viewpoints und Modellierungsaktivtäten gehören auch zur Systemarchitektur.
Problem: Alle Elemente benötigen einen ProductGeneration counter, da wir auf das Referenztsystem und die Architekturbeschreibung aller Generationen zugreifen möchten.
